result.title: Knowing Whom to Trust is not Enough: The Trust--Agreement Gap in Repeated Multi-Party LLM Negotiation
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly participate in negotiations on behalf of individuals and organizations, yet they remain vulnerable to manipulation, particularly in repeated multi-party interactions. Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon. We investigate whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and leverage them to improve future negotiation outcomes. We introduce a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement. After each game, agents assess their counterparts and maintain pairwise trust estimates that carry over to subsequent negotiations. We compare trust-aware and trust-agnostic agents and analyze how explicit trust influences negotiation outcomes. Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements. Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions. Explicit trust can therefore improve repeated LLM negotiations, but its value depends critically on how trust is assessed and incorporated into agents' reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建重复、多方、多议题的 LLM 谈判框架，让 agent 每局后评估对手并维护可跨局携带的两两信任估计，比较信任感知与不感知 agent，发现即使能在数局内识别出暗中的破坏者，准确的信任估计也未必带来更好协议，除非显式引导其使用。
AI.relevance_reason: 信任估计可视为跨轮持续更新的内部信念状态，其「估得准却不被采纳」的 trust–agreement gap 可能与 latent 状态存在却未被生成答案使用（信息坍缩、贡献分配）的问题同构，可供核查；但无视觉输入与 latent 生成机制，联系仅为概念层面。
